messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — after the RBAC tweak to the cert-rotator role this morning I started seeing TLS handshakes fail in ap-south. Not all traffic but a measurable spike.
raj.k: ugh, thanks for flagging. any logs?
maria.g: Here's the proxy log snippet from one affected box: 
```
2026-03-21T09:12:03Z proxy[ingress] WARN handshake failed: tls: failed to verify certificate chain: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-03-21T09:12:03Z proxy[ingress] ERROR fetch cert failed: keystore decrypt error: AccessDenied: KMS decrypt denied for key arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:123456789:key/abcd-rotator
```
maria.g: The cert rotator service logs show it tried to request a new cert but ACME hook failed with a 403 from the provisioner.
olivia: @raj.k did the rotator service role get the new policies? we changed RBAC for the cert-rotator k8s SA earlier.
raj.k: I updated the ClusterRoleBinding to tighten who can annotate certs. I thought that was safe, but I may have removed the service account binding for the rotator. Checking now.
sec-bot: ALERT: tls-handshake-rate +420% in ap-south over 5m window. Top affected service: ingress-proxy.
tim: if the rotator can't write the cert to the keystore, proxies will keep serving the old chain -> clients reject if intermediate is rotated. Could be PoP (proof-of-possession) step failing too.
infra-oncall: quick check: can the rotator SA call KMS decrypt in ap-south? run: `aws kms simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/cert-rotator --action-names kms:Decrypt --resource-arn arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:123456789:key/abcd-rotator`
maria.g: ran that, it returned Deny. The key policy is still allowing the principal, but the KMS grants list doesn't include the new role after the RBAC change.
raj.k: I pushed a change that removed a legacy RoleBinding to scope down access; looks like the cert-rotator SA used that binding in some clusters (ap-south only). My bad. Rolling back that binding now.
olivia: Also check audit logs — I don't see a cert issuance event in central audit for the rotator around 09:11. That suggests the cert request never got to the CA/provisioner. Audit is missing both the SA token usage and the ACME webhook call.
tim: two parallel things to validate: 1) RBAC -> ensure rotator SA can create/update secrets/annotations; 2) KMS grants -> ensure decrypt grant present for the rotator role and for the proxy service account that reads the keystore.
infra-oncall: quick mitigation: flip ingress-proxy to fallback chain and enable OCSP stapling fallback to cached staple. Patch command: `kubectl -n ingress set env ds/ingress-proxy PROXY_CERT_CHAIN=fallback && kubectl rollout restart ds/ingress-proxy`
raj.k: rollback of the RoleBinding applied at 09:20, cert-rotator restarted, I see it attempting issuance again. Logs: `INFO requesting cert for svc.example.com -> provisioner: 200 OK`.
maria.g: KMS decrypt still denied for the new cert object when rotator tries to store it: `KMS: AccessDenied` — I suspect the key grants were scoped to the old IAM role arn, not to the k8s franken-role we map to.
olivia: Did the recent IAM->k8s mapping change? we moved to IRSA mapping a month ago but touched role aliases in ap-south yesterday.
raj.k: Correct, I rotated the IAM role alias to remove a stale ARN. Looks like the grant used the exact IAM ARN rather than the role alias. I can update the KMS grant to include the new role ARN. Doing that now.
sec-bot: NOTE: audit-indexer hasn't received keystore write events from ap-south in 12m. This is abnormal.
tim: once grants are fixed we should enforce a canary: issue a short-lived cert to `canary-rotator.svc` and confirm proxies pick it up and handshake succeeds from external probe. Use `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername svc.example.com -verify_return_error`.
infra-oncall: I've applied the KMS grant change at 09:28. Rotator log -> `INFO stored cert key blob, kms-decrypt ok`. Proxy restarted and now returning full chain. External probe 09:30: `verify return:1, return code: 0 (ok)`.
maria.g: Confirming client telemetry looks normal now. Postmortem checklist: 1) make rotator RBAC changes idempotent across clusters, 2) change KMS grants to reference role alias prefix not exact ARN, 3) add audit alert when cert issuance or keystore writes drop below threshold, 4) add canary cert test to rollout job.aj.k: I'll open a PR to update ClusterRoleBinding automation and add integration tests for rotator SA across regions.
olivia: I'll add an audit rule: if no keystore writes for 10m -> pager to sec-oncall.
sec-bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED: tls-handshake-rate normalized.
maria.g: Thanks everyone. Filing a short incident note and follow-ups.
raj.k: note for postmortem - verify ACME hook permissions and ensure the provisioner returns detailed error codes in webhook responses to help triage.
maria.g: will include that. Closing thread.
